speaker: Mr Victor Lye
text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information whether the Government will consider tighter controls and real-time anomaly detection for (i) bulk SIM card purchases (ii) SIM re-registration patterns and (iii) GSM gateway misuse, given their role in enabling overseas scam calls to appear local.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The Government takes a proactive stance against scam calls and has put in place upstream controls to deter the abuse of SIM cards and GSM gateways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) has worked with the Singapore Police Force (SPF) to tighten SIM card registration rules.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The IMDA, the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) and SPF are using data analytics to detect suspicious SIM card purchase and registration patterns to prevent the misuse of SIM cards for criminal activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The import, sale and use of GSM gateways are regulated by IMDA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: The Government will continue to review and strengthen our multi-layered anti-scam measures as scam tactics evolve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
text: Those who enable scammers by providing SIM cards or GSM gateway devices will be dealt with severely under the law.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I also want to refer to the earlier Parliamentary Question, where the Minister of State made a very important point – that prevention is better than cure – in the case of scams.

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With regard to what IMDA and the Ministry is doing, may I ask two supplementary questions?

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, is there real-time monitoring – and as was referred to earlier, done as a cross-agency effort and a whole-of-Government effort – to fight scams?

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is there a real-time monitoring of unusual data usage, use of GSM gateways and so on?

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second question is, who mandates the monitoring thresholds and the data criteria?

speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is it set at the macro level or is it left to the individual telcos to determine?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Building on what Minister of State Goh Pei Ming had said earlier on the replies to the earlier two Parliamentary Questions, this is a multi-agency effort across different Government agencies – the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, the Ministry of Home Affairs, IMDA, GovTech, SPF and the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority, on the import of GSM gateways – so, it is a multi-agency effort.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On top of that, I should also mention the Monetary Authority of Singapore, which is an important player.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And on top of the multi-agency effort, it is also an effort that involves the private sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We work closely with telcos, financial institutions and banks.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We also work together with other important players, including e-commerce platforms.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is a scourge against society and it requires a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, when the Member talks about the thresholds on SIM cards and prohibition, it is something that we look at together across the different agencies – building on the data that has been collected, certainly by SPF and other agencies as well, and finding the right threshold and refining the threshold depending on the scam tactics involved.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, it is something that is not static but is dynamic, alive and something we look at on a regular basis.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Scam tactics are evolving, the bad actors are evolving; and we, the good guys, the defenders are also evolving our tactics.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In that spirit, I want to assure the Member that we are using different tools, including data analytics, to look at scam tactics and the patterns of how they are evolving.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But because of operational security considerations, we do not want the bad actors to know what we are doing.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Hence, I will not share any of the operation details.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But certainly, we are using technology, data analytics, including leveraging technologies like AI.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I also want to make two quick points.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: One, a point about the number of cases coming down.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The number of cases with phone calls as the first contact method has actually decreased, based on the recent publicly available Annual Scams and Cybercrime Briefs.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But we are not resting on our laurels and we must continue to monitor and take action.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And related to that, I know that some prevention is better than the pursuit of recovery of assets.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I know that a number of Singaporeans are also wondering: would my number and name be used to register for SIM cards by mules or by bad actors?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Persons who discover discrepancies or suspects that postpaid SIM cards have been fraudulently registered under their names should inform their telcos immediately.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, prevention is better than pursuit of losses after that.
